preliminary_shared_source_transfer.interpretation: The transfer is a useful capacity and 4K geometry candidate, but it does not address the 69.17% dense/shared Q5/Q6 wall at 512. Literal gfx1151 quant/MMQ policies remain excluded.

derived_current_efficiency.caveat: The dense/shared estimate excludes the separately attributed 147,849,216-byte router set. Encoded-equivalent rates are source-byte ledgers, not DRAM counters; cache reuse, metadata, activation traffic, and redundant loads require counter confirmation.

roofline.formula: roof wall is max(active FLOPs / 84.8 TFLOP/s, source bytes under stated one-scan policy / 729.067 GB/s); attention adds the existing 5.084 TFLOP 4K QK+PV ledger
caveats: All-expert source bytes are a conservative upper bound for one compacted chunk; a retained routed-MMQ candidate must publish routing-aware distinct-expert bytes and physical counters.
The compute reference is a dense BF16 WMMA ceiling; IQ integer-dot and dequantized K-quant kernels require their own measured achieved rate.
Model load, lm-head single-row work, activation bytes, quantization, and non-linear kernels are outside the simplified max-of-floors model.

llama_cpp_review.hip: For rows above the <=8 MMVQ cutoff, ggml-cuda/HIP selects mul_mat_q, quantizes source rows once to layout-qualified Q8_1, compacts/scatters MUL_MAT_ID rows, and launches RDNA-family 256-thread MMQ tiles for Q5_K/Q6_K/IQ2_XS/IQ3_XXS/IQ4_XS. Gate/up broadcast quantization is deduplicated before top-k scatter.
llama_cpp_review.vulkan: The audited RADV routed comparator uses the medium local128/two-wave64 64-column x 64-row K32 MMQ, stages quant/activation tiles, and reuses each loaded weight across many prompt rows. Literal subgroup/tile constants do not transfer to wave32 HIP.
llama_cpp_review.hipengine_gap: The control dense/shared gguf_k_prefill_out kernels launch one output-column owner per prompt row (Grid_Size_Y=128), so the same Q5/Q6 weight is reread for every row. The first port seam is exact grid-y row batching/MMQ, not another attention variant.

transfer_lessons: gfx1151 is a hypothesis source, not a geometry oracle: its 256-row Qwen chunk policy regressed gfx1100 by 6.4-8.8%.
Compiler/resource behavior is architecture-local: a fully unrolled selected-MoE body spilled at 256 VGPR on gfx1100 until outer-loop rolling removed spills.
Some launch seams transfer independently: router logits 512->256 threads, router select 512->128, and stream-ordered metadata won on gfx1100 after their own gates.
Wave widening is not monotonic: gfx1151 retained four-wave Q8 through 64K, while gfx1100 retained two-wave only through 4K.
Counterbalanced process order is mandatory for small wins; the gfx1151 AOTriton queue screen changed verdict after reverse-order and 15-sample measurement.
Reprofile immediately after each promotion; for Q2 XL the short priority is dense/shared Q5/Q6, then routed IQ MMQ, then attention.
next_order: Exact dense/shared raw-Q5/Q6 row reuse: extend the existing small-B exact rowtile premise to fixed grid-y row batches, measure natural K3072/K6144/K9216 and output widths, then full 512/4K.
If exact row batching remains below target, add source-faithful Q8_1 integer MMQ for Q5/Q6 with bounded quality gates and no persistent sidecar.
Port routed IQ2/IQ3/IQ4 compact MMQ with producer-row quantization before top-10 expansion and expert-major tiles; publish distinct-expert and physical traffic.
Reprofile; only then optimize short attention or launch/fusion residuals.
Do not run 16K/64K/128K until the 512>=400 and 4096>=300 exact repeated gate passes; do not reopen the full long campaign before 512>=800 and 4096>=700 or a measured roofline blocker is documented.
